title: Companion terminal runner and custom keys
description: Opens real tmux panes from the Companion Terminals tab: a pane whose process the gateway matches to a runner shows that runner row, an unmatched pane stays generic, a saved runner choice overrides auto detection until cleared, and a device-level custom key is added, sent, kept across reopening and deleted. Key taps are checked against the bytes the pane received.

proofTargets.claim: The gateway lists processRunnerIds only for a pane whose process matches a runner safe to identify without a recorded identity.
A known-runner pane shows the runner row and a tap sends that key data to the pane.
An unmatched pane shows the generic keys and no runner row.
A saved runner choice for a pane wins over its detected runner until cleared, then detection applies again.
A palette key added in the terminal shows in a Yours row, sends its palette data, survives reopening the terminal and is removed by delete.

setup.intent: Create two byte-recording tmux panes and check that the slot gateway derives a runner only for the one whose process is named like a runner binary.

hud-known.intent: Pane running a claude binary: the gateway process match should pick its runner row.

refresh-terminals.intent: Reload the pane list so it includes the two new panes.

known-row.intent: Wait for the runner-named pane in the Terminals list and read its row label.

press-known-row.intent: Open the runner-named pane from its row.

wait-known-screen.intent: The worker terminal is on screen.

wait-known-profile.intent: The key bar names the runner taken from the gateway process match.

wait-known-row.intent: The runner row renders below the generic keys.

hide-hud-known.intent: Hide the HUD so every key row is fully visible in the capture.

capture-known.label: Known runner pane with its runner row
capture-known.intent: Record the generic keys, the tmux toggle and the runner row together.

hud-runner-tap.intent: Tap History on the runner row; the pane has to receive 0x12.

press-runner-key.intent: Send the History shortcut from the runner row to the pane.

assert-runner-bytes.intent: The pane received exactly that key data (0x12) through the worker input call.

hud-override.intent: Save Pi for this pane over its detected runner, then return to auto.

open-picker.intent: Open the runner key picker for this pane.

pick-pi.intent: Save a runner choice for this pane.

wait-saved-profile.intent: The saved choice wins over the process match.

wait-saved-row.intent: The row switches to the four Pi keys.

hide-hud-saved.intent: Hide the HUD so every key row is fully visible in the capture.

capture-saved.label: Saved Pi choice on the detected Claude Code pane
capture-saved.intent: Record the row the saved choice selects over detection.

hud-clear-choice.intent: Clear the saved runner so the pane returns to auto detection.

wait-auto-again.intent: Clearing the choice returns the pane to its detected runner.

auto-row-gone.intent: The row is back to the three Claude Code keys.

hud-unknown.intent: Pane running keysink: no runner match, so only the generic keys.

back-from-known.intent: Go back to the Terminals tab.

unknown-row.intent: Wait for the unmatched pane in the Terminals list and read its row label.

press-unknown-row.intent: Open the pane whose process matches no runner.

wait-unknown-profile.intent: With no linked run and no process match the key bar stays generic.

no-runner-row.intent: No runner keys render for this pane.

generic-keys.intent: The generic terminal keys stay available.

no-custom-row-yet.intent: Start from a device with no saved keys of its own.

hide-hud-unknown.intent: Hide the HUD so every key row is fully visible in the capture.

capture-unknown.label: Unknown pane: generic keys only
capture-unknown.intent: Record the generic row without a runner row or a Yours row.

hud-custom.intent: Add a device key from the palette (Alt+Left, flagged danger) and send it.

open-manage.intent: Open the editor for keys of your own.

close-keyboard.intent: Close the keyboard so the whole palette is in view.

pick-palette.intent: Pick a modified arrow from the palette.

mark-danger.intent: Flag the new key as dangerous.

wait-custom-row.intent: A Yours row renders even though this pane has no runner row.

wait-custom-label.intent: The new key carries its trimmed label.

hide-hud-custom.intent: Hide the HUD so every key row is fully visible in the capture.

capture-custom.label: Yours row with a danger-styled key
capture-custom.intent: Record the Yours row and the danger style on the new key.

hud-custom-tap.intent: Tap the new key; the pane has to receive its Alt+Left sequence.

press-custom-key.intent: Send the new Alt+Left key from the Yours row to the pane.

assert-custom-bytes.intent: The pane received the palette sequence for Alt+Left through the worker input call.

hud-reopen.intent: Leave and reopen the terminal: the saved key has to persist.

back-from-unknown.intent: Leave the terminal for the Terminals tab.

unknown-row-again.intent: Back on the Terminals tab: read the same pane row again.

wait-custom-kept.intent: The saved key is still there after reopening.

hide-hud-reopened.intent: Hide the HUD so every key row is fully visible in the capture.

capture-reopened.label: Yours row after reopening the terminal
capture-reopened.intent: Record the key surviving a fresh terminal screen.

hud-delete.intent: Delete the key: its row goes away.

custom-row-gone.intent: The Yours row is gone once its last key is deleted.

hide-hud-deleted.intent: Hide the HUD so every key row is fully visible in the capture.

capture-deleted.label: Yours row removed after delete
capture-deleted.intent: Record the terminal after deleting the key.

hud-pass.intent: Runner row, generic row, saved choice and device keys all checked.
